rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Two non-zero vectors are collinear (parallel) when one is a scalar multiple of the other, so their cross product is zero and their component ratios are equal. Non-collinear vectors are linearly independent in a plane and can serve as a basis for every vector in that plane.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
b = λa (λ ∈ ℝ) ⇔ a ∥ b
a × b = 0 ⇔ a ∥ b (for non-zero a, b)
(x₁, y₁) ∥ (x₂, y₂) ⇔ x₁y₂ − x₂y₁ = 0

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Assuming equal lengths imply parallel vectors; direction, not magnitude, decides collinearity.  ·  Dividing by a zero component when comparing ratios; use cross multiplication instead.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: A line through point a with direction d has vector equation r = a + td; collinearity is the statement that two points share such a direction d.  ·  Unit vectors give direction only: â = a/|a|; collinear vectors have either equal or opposite unit vectors.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Are (1, 2, 3) and (2, 4, 6) collinear? Ratios 2/1 = 4/2 = 6/3 = 2, so the second is 2× the first; yes, same direction.  ·  Find k such that a = (k, 3) and b = (4, 6) are parallel. k·6 − 4·3 = 0 ⇒ 6k = 12 ⇒ k = 2.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: The zero vector is parallel to every vector by convention, so exclude it from direction arguments.  ·  A negative scalar multiple reverses direction but preserves the line of action.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Classify six vector pairs  ·  Solve three section-formula problems

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Cross-multiply component pairs instead of dividing, so zero components never break the test.  ·  For 2-D vectors (x₁, y₁) and (x₂, y₂), check x₁y₂ − x₂y₁ = 0 as a one-line parallel test.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Determine whether (2, −1, 4) and (−4, 2, −8) are parallel, and state the scalar.  ·  Find k if points (1, 2), (3, k) and (5, 8) are collinear.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: State the non-zero condition before using a × b = 0.  ·  For collinear points, always work with AB and AC, then conclude about A, B, C.

rows.text: Any set containing the zero vector is linearly dependent.  ·  In three dimensions three non-coplanar vectors form a basis of ℝ³.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: **Collinearity.** Non-zero vectors a and b are collinear iff b = λa for some real scalar λ; λ > 0 means the same direction, λ < 0 the opposite direction.  ·  **Component test.** For a = (a₁, a₂, a₃) and b = (b₁, b₂, b₃), collinearity means a₁/b₁ = a₂/b₂ = a₃/b₃ wherever the denominators are non-zero; handle zero components by cross multiplication instead of division.  ·  **Cross-product test.** a and b are parallel exactly when a × b = 0. This works in both two and three dimensions (embed a 2-D vector as (x, y, 0)).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: p = (n·a + m·b)/(m + n) for AP : PB = m : n  ·  [a b c] = a · (b × c) = 0 ⇔ a, b, c coplanar  ·  Collinearity of points is tested with displacement vectors, not position vectors.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Two non-zero vectors are collinear if and only if their cross product vanishes.  ·  Two non-collinear vectors in a plane form a basis for that plane.  ·  Three points are collinear exactly when the triangle they form has zero area.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: To prove three points collinear, show AB = λ AC rather than comparing all three position vectors.  ·  Plot three pairs of 2-D vectors and classify each as parallel, opposite, or non-collinear.  ·  Verify that (1, 1) and (2, −1) span every vector in the plane by solving for general (p, q).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Worked example.** a = (2, −3, 1) and b = (−6, 9, −3) give ratios −6/2 = 9/(−3) = −3/1 = −3, so b = −3a and the vectors are anti-parallel.  ·  **Non-collinear.** If no single scalar λ satisfies b = λa, the vectors are non-collinear; in a plane two non-collinear vectors are linearly independent.  ·  **Linear independence.** αa + βb = 0 forces α = β = 0 when a and b are non-collinear; for collinear vectors non-trivial choices exist, e.g. α = λ, β = −1.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Basis of a plane.** Any vector r in the plane of two non-collinear vectors a, b can be written uniquely as r = xa + yb; the coefficients (x, y) are the coordinates in that basis.  ·  **Section formula.** If point P divides AB in the ratio m : n, then p = (n·a + m·b)/(m + n); the midpoint case m = n gives p = (a + b)/2.  ·  **Collinear points.** Three points A, B, C are collinear iff AB and AC are parallel, i.e. AB × AC = 0, or equivalently the area of triangle ABC is zero.
